body_markdown:
In a new article for Route Fifty, NextNav’s Deepak Joseph explores why America needs a reliable GPS complement and backup, and how California is helping lead the way. The world’s first ground-based, 5G-powered 3D positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) network is currently being tested in Santa Clara County, demonstrating the potential of complementary technology to strengthen America’s PNT resilience.


GPS is too critical to leave without a backup. Building a more resilient PNT ecosystem is essential to protecting the systems, services, and infrastructure Americans depend on every day.


“ *Silicon Valley is an ideal place to show how a new layer of PNT resilience can work in the real world. Santa Clara County is also a microcosm of the types of environments where we need this technology to excel. It’s a complex environment with a dense downtown, an airport and millions of commercial wireless connections. If the system can work there, it can work anywhere. The ongoing testing validates the value of this technology, which can be delivered by cellular networks more broadly across the U.S.* “


Read the full article[here](https://www.route-fifty.com/emerging-tech/2026/11/america-needs-gps-backup-and-california-leads-way/417117/) .
